# Happy-path tests

@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "s1, s2, expected",
    [
        ("kitten", "sitting", 3),      # classic example
        ("flaw", "lawn", 2),
        ("intention", "execution", 5),
        ("book", "back", 2),
        ("", "", 0),                   # both empty
        ("abc", "abc", 0),             # identical strings
        ("abc", "ab", 1),              # single deletion
        ("ab", "abc", 1),              # single insertion (triggers recursion branch)
        ("café", "cafe", 1),           # unicode, accent difference
    ],
)
def test_levenshtein_happy_path(s1, s2, expected):
    assert levenshtein(s1, s2) == expected
    # Distance should always be an int
    assert isinstance(levenshtein(s1, s2), int)

def test_levenshtein_empty_vs_nonempty():
    assert levenshtein("", "abcd") == 4
    assert levenshtein("abcd", "") == 4


def test_levenshtein_long_string_difference_of_one():
    """Very long strings that differ by exactly one character."""
    s1 = "x" * 10_000
    s2 = "x" * 9_999
    assert levenshtein(s1, s2) == 1


@pytest.mark.parametrize(

        ("longer string here", "short"),

def test_levenshtein_symmetry(s1, s2):
    """Distance must be symmetric: d(a, b) == d(b, a)."""
    assert levenshtein(s1, s2) == levenshtein(s2, s1)
